newsitem.title: EGYPT: Popular mills, cement stocks boost Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Popular mills, cement stocks boost Cairo bourse.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to scale new heights on Monday, with popular milling and cement shares taking the lead, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index closed at 262.60 points, 2.06 higher than Sunday's all-time record of 260.54.
Turnover was a high 76.12 million pounds ($22.39). The listing of recently privatised shares in Cairo Pharmaceuticals and Chemicals Industries accounted for 48.85 million of that total.
The state offered investors 708,000 shares of the firm's 3.54 million shares at a minimum of 40 pounds a share for three days from November 19.
The privatised shares opened on the stock exchange at 46.00 pounds. Ahmed el-Helw of EFG/Hermes brokerage said share allocation was 39 percent for individuals and 12 percent for mutual funds.
"The market was very active today. It's still going in a good direction but the relatively small rise in the index was good because this small correction allows the market to gain depth," he said.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the day's most actively traded stock, rising 2.56 to close at 70.56 in turnover of more than 5.70 million pounds.
East Delta Flour Mills climbed 6.70 percent to close at 53.50 after trading in shares worth more than 1.70 million pounds.

Suez Cement traded in shares worth almost three million pounds but the stock ended 2.50 pounds lower at 55. Egyptian Tora Portland Cement rose 1.30 to 69.30 in turnover of more than 2.50 million pounds.
Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals was the day's biggest gainer, jumping 23 percent to close at 80 pounds from Sunday's 65.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 392.78 from 392.42 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 185.26 from 183.07.
